text:
julia: heads-up: nightly-smoke on the rtx6000 pool is red — warmup step OOM + GPU kernel crash on 2/4 shards. attaching quick logs below.

ci-bot: test run smoke-rtx6000-4532 failed (exit 137). logs: https://ci.internal/runs/4532 :warning:

mike: can you paste the tail of the launcher log? suspect driver skew after the infra rollout.

julia: paste: ```[2026-04-02 07:20:43] gpu0: cudaErrorUnknown: Xid 86: GPU kernel error, process killed
...OOM allocating 2.1GB for kv cache
stack: /usr/lib/libcuda.so.1(+0x7f3b0)
[2026-04-02 07:20:43] warmup: exit status 137
```

rahul: which driver/kernel combo on that node? can you run `nvidia-smi` and `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version`?

julia: node rtx-ct-05 -> NVIDIA Driver 535.86, CUDA 12.2, kernel 6.1. infra note: canary started rolling driver 536.* yesterday.

mike: that explains it. CI images are still built against 535 ABI. two options: pin nodes back to 535 for smoke, or repro with 536 locally.

rahul: filed a quick rerun: `@ci-bot rerun smoke-rtx6000-4532 --force-image=driver-535-tag`

ci-bot: Rerun queued: smoke-rtx6000-4532-rerun-2 (scheduled on rtx-ct-01..rtx-ct-08) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

julia: if rerun fails I'll escalate to bisect — I suspect driver 536 changed kernel launch alignment or allocator behavior causing small allocations to die on warmup.

sre: FYI I've pinned the smoke pool label to driver-535 to reduce noisy infra noise while we triage.

mike: if rerun still fails, please collect `dmesg` + NVML traces and upload to /tmp/rtx-ct-05-debug.tar.gz and paste link here. I'll take a look at the kernel stack.

julia: will grab traces if needed. thanks. :thumbsup:

rahul: also pinging @eng-infra for possible auto-rollback if we hit >3 smoke failures in 30m (to avoid cascading flakes).

sre: noted, creating alert threshold and watching the rerun.

julia: quick note for reviewers: i'm going to hold merging any perf/allocator PRs until we confirm driver stability. will update this thread.
